newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM says reforms top priority of new cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Russia PM says reforms top priority of new cabinet.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Cheronmyrdin said on Tuesday that pursuing economic reforms would be the top priority of his reshuffled cabinet.

"The main task of the government will be broadening and speeding up reforms in the social and economic spheres. Their implementation is our top priority," Interfax news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as saying.
"The situation in the country has to be changed quickly for the better and all conditions for this have now been created," he added.
Over the past two weeks President Boris Yeltsin has drafted several young liberals into prominent cabinet positions in an effort to jump-start Russia's flagging economic reform process.

The new appointments include Anatoly Chubais, architect of Russian privatisation who is now a first deputy premier and finance minister, and Boris Nemtsov, a leading regional pro-reform governor who takes charge of social programmes and natural monopolies. Nemtsov is also a first deputy premier.

"The president hopes that the new government -- a united and to a great extent renewed team -- will work together on normalising the situation in the country, especially in the social sphere," Interfax quoted Kremlin press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying on Tuesday.

Chernomyrdin presented Chubais to his new staff at the finance ministry and said the ministry would have to give urgent attention to the issue of unpaid wages and pensions -- a painful issue for millions of Russians.

Defending his previous government's record, he said the integrity of the state and political stability had been preserved in the face of tough economic conditions and added that budget targets for 1996 had largely been met.
"This year's budget will be hard to fulfil, but we will have to manage. The people joining the government now are aimed at (fulfilling the budget's targets)," Chernomyrdin said.
